title: Soft White Bread 2 (Tangzhong)
description: A soft, airy loaf with a tender crumb, made using tangzhong and hand-rolled sections for perfect pull-apart texture.

ingredients.notes: divided: 30g for Tangzhong, 560g for Main Dough
divided: 190ml for Tangzhong, 180ml for Main Dough

method.instruction: Make the tangzhong: in a small saucepan, combine 30 g of the bread flour and 190 ml of the water. Cook over medium heat, whisking constantly, until thickened to approximately 65°C. Remove from heat and let cool to room temperature.
In a large bowl, combine the remaining 560 g of bread flour, salt, bread improver, yeast, and sugar.

Add the cooled tangzhong, the remaining 180 ml of water, and 20 ml of vegetable oil. Mix until a rough dough forms, then knead for 10–12 minutes until smooth and elastic. Dust hands lightly if sticky, but avoid drying the dough out.
Place dough in a lightly oiled bowl, cover, and let rise in a warm place until doubled in size, about 1–1½ hours.
Gently punch down the dough and knead briefly to redistribute air for a finer crumb.
Divide dough into three equal portions. Roll each into a ball, then cup in one hand and tuck edges underneath while rotating gently to create a smooth, taut dome.
Place the balls snugly into a greased loaf tin approximately 8 cm × 18 cm, edges touching lightly.
Cover loosely and let rise until puffed and slightly jiggly, about 45–60 minutes.
Lightly brush the top of the dough with 60 ml full-cream milk before baking.
Bake for 25–30 minutes. If browning is slow, increase to 190°C for the last few minutes.
Remove from oven and immediately brush the warm loaf with 30 g of melted unsalted butter.
Let the loaf rest for 5–10 minutes in the tin, then lift out and cool slightly before slicing.

notes.title: The Tension Trick
notes.content: Cupping each dough ball and tucking the edges underneath while rotating creates a taut surface that holds its shape during baking and prevents sagging sides.

notes.title: Flour Choice
notes.content: Wallaby's bread flour gives a softer, smoother dough and a better rise compared to plain flour. Bread flour with 12–14% protein is recommended.

notes.title: Milk and Butter Finish
notes.content: Brushing with milk before baking gives a soft, golden crust. Brushing with melted butter after baking adds flavour and a glossy finish.
